attempts.note: scope "/collections" in the Lightning router has exactly six routes (GET/POST/DELETE /:name, GET/PUT/DELETE /:name/:key) plus a NoRoute catch-all; all six are modelled. Shapes read from collections_controller.ex, Lightning.Collections.Item's Jason encoder and LightningWeb.API.Filters.collection_items/1.
Vendor API.md covers the error format shared with /collections; it lists only the collection-management routes under /api, not the item routes.
The only OpenAPI Lightning ships covers workflows, not collections.
401: the path matches GET /:name (a collection called openapi.json) and asks for a token; it is not a spec route. No openapi/swagger file in OpenFn/lightning or OpenFn/adaptors packages/collections.
Prose usage docs for the adaptor (keys, wildcards, limits); no HTTP reference.
Only a community "OpenFn Lightning API" workspace, not vendor-published, no collections routes.

notes: Lightning's Collections API: the six item routes under /collections on an OpenFn Lightning instance, which is everything the collections adaptor (0.9.4) can reach - it builds paths only under configuration.collections_endpoint. Synthesized from the vendor source (router.ex scope "/collections", CollectionsController, Item encoder, Filters) and cross-checked against the adaptor's get/set/remove/each and its bundled mock; ast.json is empty because the operations live in the collections namespace. Complete: the route set is finite and every route is modelled, including PUT /{name}/{key} which Lightning serves but the adaptor never calls. Corrections over the July stub: removed the invented GET / listCollections (the router has no such route; it 404s), added the updated_after/updated_before filters and the created/updated item timestamps the server returns, and documented that the server ignores date filters on DELETE /{name}. Errors are RFC 9457 problem documents on Lightning main; v2.20.1 answers some failures with {upserted: 0, error: "..."} instead. Collection creation/renaming is in the openfn spec (/api/projects/{project_id}/collections/{id}).
